scope.purpose: Navigate to another page or resource from inside text, as an underlined word or phrase that reads with the sentence around it and tells the reader what it leads to (a page, another site, an email, a phone number, a file and its format, a printable version).
useCases: A link inside a paragraph, a help text, a table cell or a message, taking the surrounding typography.
A standalone text link (See all, Learn more) placed by the layout, still underlined.
A destination announced before the click: another site (new tab, arrow), an email address (envelope), a phone number (handset), a printable version (printer).
A link to a file showing its format and size as text and a format glyph: Annual report (PDF, 2.4 MB).
A link inside a colored context (status message, inverse surface) that keeps the context color with tone inherit.
exclusions: Navigation to a task with a control appearance: Button with href.
Opening the print dialog, sending a form, copying an address: actions, so Button (with a leading Icon).
A disabled link: a destination that cannot be followed is plain text.
Free leading or trailing icons: the indicator is chosen by destination.
Distinct visited color; size or weight options (the context decides typography).
Formatting file sizes or detecting the format from href: the application passes fileType and fileSize.
Routing: the application's router intercepts navigation; the component renders a native link.
alternatives: Button (with href) for a call to action or navigation to a task.
IconButton (with href) for an icon-only navigation control.
Breadcrumb, Tabs, Pagination (wave 4) for structured navigation.

versions.bitsUi: not used (a native anchor carries the semantics)

contract.scope: Link contract: required label and href, tone (accent, inherit), destination (page, external, email, phone, file, print) with fileType, fileSize and destinationLabel; container, label, meta and indicator parts; default, hover and pressed interaction with focus; color.content.link, underline widths, indicator gap and focus roles; thirteen rules (destinations and glyphs, file meta, accessible name and suffix, permanent underline, tone, wrapping, no disabled state, focus per line box, forced colors). The dark link color amendment (accent.300) is recorded in the semantic approval.

decisionsTaken: label is a required string, like Button, rather than free children: the accessible name is then known to the component (needed to append the external suffix) and Figma maps it to a text property.

Underlined in every state (WCAG 1.4.1, use of color): the hover and pressed feedback thickens the underline from border.width.default (1 px) to border.width.strong (2 px) instead of changing the color, so no new color token is needed; no transition.
One color role, color.content.link (approved), and tone inherit for colored contexts; no visited color in an application context.
No size prop and no typography role: a link takes the font of the text it sits in.
Focus indicator drawn around each line box (an outline, so a wrapped link gets one ring per line) with radius.indicator corners: radius.focus (concentric with controls) is too round for text.
No Bits UI primitive: a native anchor carries every semantic needed.

User review of the contract drafts (2026-10-16): the trailing indicator orients the reader on what the link leads to. The boolean external becomes destination (page, external, email, phone, file, print) with fileType and fileSize for files; externalLabel becomes destinationLabel (overrides the default English suffix of any destination).
phone added beside email (tel: links are the same kind of destination); print means a link to a printable version, because opening the print dialog is an action that belongs to Button.

File links show the format and size as visible text (PDF, 2.4 MB) in addition to the format glyph: the small lettering inside Phosphor's file glyphs is not legible at text size, and visible text helps everyone, not only screen reader users (practice of GOV.UK and most public-sector systems). The component does not format sizes (locale) and sets no download attribute: viewable formats open in the browser, others download, as the server decides.

Glyphs (Phosphor, MIT): ArrowUpRight, Envelope, Phone, Printer, File, FilePdf, FileDoc, FileXls, FileCsv, FilePpt, FileTxt, FileZip, FileImage, FileAudio, FileVideo, copied as inline SVG paths into the component folder per the icon decision; one em square so they follow the text size. Only external opens a new tab.
No new token: meta and indicator take the link color; indicatorGap is space.content.xs.

User at the contract gate (2026-10-17): destinations confirmed as drafted (phone included, print = a link to a printable version); dark link color changed to color.palette.accent.300 (4.80:1 or more on every neutral backdrop in the 18 contexts; recommendation A).

openDecisions.question: Should a file link (or any destination) also be able to open in a new tab, announced like external?
openDecisions.proposal: Not in v1: only external opens a new tab; a PDF opens in the browser tab and Back returns. A newTab option can be added later if products need it.

nextAction: Implementation gate (grouped with the other components of the wave): the reviewer exercises the preview page; record the approval with source digests, then the Figma parity phase (ggb-figma).
implementationNotes: Markup: <a class="ggb-link" data-tone data-destination href> with the label, a <span class="ggb-link__meta"> for files, the glyph (aria-hidden) and a visually hidden suffix; external adds target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer". The last word, meta and glyph are wrapped in a no-wrap span so they never start a line alone.
Underline through text-decoration (thickness from the tokens, text-underline-offset from-font) on the label only; focus with outline on the inline box so it follows each line.
Glyph table in a glyphs.ts of the component folder, keyed by destination and normalized fileType.

Implemented: the underline is drawn on the label spans (not the anchor) so that meta and glyph are never underlined; box-decoration-break: clone for per-line corners and focus ring; rel merged with noopener noreferrer for external; target owned. Glyph table copied from @phosphor-icons/core 2.1.1.
